name: Boeing AH-64E Apache Guardian (India)

header.one_liner: India operates the Boeing AH-64E Apache attack helicopter across two services — 22 with the IAF (inducted 2019) and 6 with the Indian Army (fleet completed December 2025) — while Tata Boeing Aerospace in Hyderabad is Boeing's global sole-source producer of Apache fuselages.

what_it_is.prose: The Boeing AH-64E Apache Guardian is India's frontline attack helicopter, now in service with two branches of the armed forces. The Indian Air Force's order for 22 AH-64E was finalised as part of a September 2015 Boeing contract (alongside 15 CH-47F Chinooks); the IAF formally inducted the type on 3 September 2019 at Air Force Station Pathankot, with all 22 delivered by 2020, replacing the ageing Mi-35 fleet. A separate 2020 contract added six AH-64E for the Indian Army; Boeing began delivering these in July 2025 and the Indian Army completed its six-aircraft fleet in December 2025, basing them at Jodhpur under the 451 Army Aviation Squadron. Boeing states that India operates 22 AH-64 Apaches with six more on order for the Army, alongside 11 C-17s, 15 CH-47 Chinooks and 12 P-8Is. India's principal industrial stake in the programme is manufacturing rather than integration: Tata Boeing Aerospace Limited (TBAL) in Hyderabad is Boeing's global sole-source producer of Apache fuselages, having delivered the first Indian Army Apache fuselage on 19 January 2023 and supplied over 190 fuselages to Boeing's Mesa, Arizona final-assembly line, with more than 90% of component parts sourced from over 100 Indian MSMEs. The Atlas treats the Apache as a foreign-origin (US) platform in Indian service with a documented Indian aerostructure role, without converting local fuselage work into an unsupported indigenous-content percentage.

deployments_procurement.summary: India acquired the Apache through two US Foreign Military Sales: 22 AH-64E for the IAF (order finalised September 2015, inducted September 2019, complete by 2020) and 6 AH-64E for the Indian Army (contract 2020, delivered July–December 2025, based at Jodhpur). The IAF fleet replaced the Mi-35. India's industrial role centres on TBAL Hyderabad, the global sole-source Apache fuselage producer.

import_dependencies.summary: The Apache is a US-origin Boeing platform acquired via Foreign Military Sales. While TBAL in Hyderabad is the global sole-source producer of the Apache fuselage, final integration, engines, sensors, fire-control radar and weapons are US-supplied, so the delivered aircraft remains an import-dependent platform.

faq.question: How many Apaches does India operate and with which services?
faq.answer: India operates 28 AH-64E Apaches across two services: 22 with the Indian Air Force (inducted September 2019 at Pathankot, complete by 2020) and 6 with the Indian Army (contract 2020, first three delivered July 2025 and the final three in December 2025, based at Jodhpur under 451 Army Aviation Squadron).

faq.question: What is India's manufacturing role in the Apache programme?
faq.answer: Tata Boeing Aerospace Limited (TBAL) in Hyderabad is Boeing's global sole-source producer of Apache fuselages. It delivered the first Indian Army Apache fuselage on 19 January 2023 and has supplied over 190 fuselages to Boeing's Mesa, Arizona final-assembly line, with more than 90% of parts from over 100 Indian MSMEs.

faq.question: Is the Apache indigenous to India?
faq.answer: No. The AH-64E is a US-origin Boeing platform acquired through Foreign Military Sales. India's fuselages are made in Hyderabad by TBAL, but final integration, engines, fire-control radar, sensors and weapons are all US-supplied, so the delivered aircraft is a foreign-origin platform.
